newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq gives U.N. data on chemical weapons- papers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq gives U.N. data on chemical weapons- papers.

text.p: Iraq has given the U.N.'s chief arms inspector a detailed report on its chemical weapons, newspapers said on Sunday.

Quoting a Foreign Ministry spokesman, they also said Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz had agreed with Rolf Ekeus, head of the U.N. Special Commission in charge of Iraq's post-Gulf War disarmament, to speed up work on the biological weapons issue.

Ekeus said on Saturday in Baghdad after three days of talks with Aziz that he had told Iraq he needed to resolve "seven important issues...If we manage to settle them we will come close to...ending the chemical file programme."
He said he still had serious concerns over Iraq's biological warfare programme.
"The chemical file was discussed and the Iraqi side has submitted a detailed report answering again questions raised by the Special Commission," al-Qadissiya quoted the spokesman as saying.
"Both sides have discussed the biological file and agreed on a joint working formula to conclude the...file," it added.
"It has been agreed to solve all practical problems within the framework of cooperation."

Ekeus also said on Saturday that Baghdad was obstructing flights by U.N. helicopters, sometimes going so far as to risk the lives of pilots and experts on board. He said Aziz had pledged to address the matter.
But on Sunday the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said Ekeus was imagining things.
"Ekeus's statements are based on...imagination," it said, adding that he was trying to prolong his work: "His behaviour gives the impression that there is a personal financial benefit."
